text:
B: Hi! Sorry, hi. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Gemma.
B: I'm Chloe. Erm, is this your last one as well?
A: Hope so. I've got dinner to sort, well, Craig has.
B: Oh, is that the Craig from the... sorry, no, there's a Craig in this, isn't there?
A: Different Craig. Mine's my husband. Unfortunately for him.
B: Ha. Erm, so what do you do?
A: Warehouse. Site ops manager. You're a student, yeah? Teaching?
B: Yeah! Primary. How did everyone guess that?
A: You look like a teacher. It's the bookshelf.
B: That's fair, actually. They're all picture books. I'm third year, so last placement's coming up, which I'm kind of dreading, to be honest.
A: Why? You'll be fine. It's kids.
B: It's not the kids. It's more being watched. My mentor on my second year one was, erm, quite harsh. She'd sit at the back with a clipboard and then at the end she'd go through everything I'd done wrong, like a list. I sort of went to pieces a bit after one of them. Sorry, that's probably a bit much.
A: No. ...I'm probably that mentor, if I'm honest.
B: Oh no!
A: Well, I am. I'll tell someone it's not good enough in front of their whole shift. Staff don't love me for it.
B: Erm. Does it work, though?
A: Sometimes. Sometimes they just go off sick.
B: Right.
A: You've got to have a thick skin, that's all I'm saying. People will have a go. Doesn't mean you're rubbish.
B: Yeah. That's kind of what my mum says. She's a hairdresser, she gets moaned at all day.
A: There you go. What year d'you want?
B: Key Stage 1, ideally. Year 1 or 2. They're so little, they just tell you everything.
A: My boy's nine. Year 5. Got a letter on the fridge about some Viking day I haven't read yet.
B: Oh, they love a Viking day. You'll probably need a costume.
A: Brilliant. Craig'll do it. He does the school stuff, I'm never there for it. Hours are all over the place.
B: That's really normal, though. Loads of the parents on placement were like that, the dads did drop-off. The kids don't mind, honestly, they just want someone there.
A: Hm. Is that the teacher voice?
B: Sorry, a bit. My dad's an electrician, so he was always the one who could pick us up, 'cause he could fit jobs round it.
A: Craig's a sparky. Self-employed.
B: No way! My dad's self-employed as well. Does he moan about the VAT?
A: Every quarter. Without fail.
B: That's my dad! He goes in the shed and swears at the laptop.
A: That's every electrician in the country, that.
B: Ha. Erm, have you got a dog? I thought I saw one in your photo.
A: Biscuit. Cockapoo. Chewed through my charger this morning, so that's my morning.
B: Aw, ours is a Staffie, she's really old, she just snores on the landi—
